h: Shabbos and the Power of Answering Amen With All Strength

p: in which is the life of all
and may it rise up to the head."
"Bound up in the bundle of life with Hashem your God";
that is, what is secondary to the Name Havayah.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר סִימָן כ״ט
And as is written in Sefer HaBahir, section 29,
that from it all the souls fly forth.
for this attribute, the attribute of Malchus,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קעב, א)
that through it the work of the world is done.
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רכ, א)
And in the holy Zohar (this parsha, Zohar III 220a):
do it with your strength, etc." (Koheles 9:10).
"How fitting it is for a person,
to exert himself and to do
the will of his Master, etc."
הַיְינוּ נֵר ה׳ נִשְׁמַת אָדָם (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז)
means "the lamp of Hashem is the soul of man" (Mishlei 20:27);
"And a lamp is lit for him over his head,
and he gazes and looks by it
from one end of the world to the other,
'When His lamp shone over my head.'"
which is from the first light,
by which man used to gaze
from one end of the world to the other
is the strength that rests upon him,
and about this it is written (Bamidbar 14:17):
'Let the strength of my Lord be great';
this is the strength that rests upon the tzaddikim."
And this is why before it is said "And now" (Bamidbar 14:17),
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה כא, ו)
which is along the lines of what they said (Bereishis Rabbah 21:6):
For so the expression "and now" indicates,
that from now on the matter will change for the good.
"let the strength of Hashem be great."
And this is the meaning of
"may its strength increase and may it rise up to the head";
it is based on what is said
until he had grown old, etc.;
enter at once and cleave to Him,
to the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.,
because they are closer to the King
with greater longing of the heart
And this is "may its strength increase":
that the strength of Hashem grow great;
"and may it rise up to the head"
by which one enters the supernal days,
which are the first three Sefiros,
like Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
for he merited the attribute of Atika Kadisha.
one must do the will of your Master,
'for there is no deed or reckoning, etc.'"
"for there is no deed or reckoning
וְדַעַת וְחָכְמָה בִּשְׁאוֹל וְגוֹ׳ (קֹהֶלֶת ט, י)
or knowledge or wisdom in the grave, etc." (Koheles 9:10).
"Your strength" is the strength of Hashem,
And it is found in the holy Zohar
(פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנז, א)
from the side of the three supernal levels,
and she is the daughter, fourth to them, etc."
for it is the beginning of "your strength,"
which is to stir up the good inclination
whose power is to make a person forget everything,
וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (נְדָרִים לב, ב)
similar to what is written in the Gemara (Nedarim 32b)
that at the time of the evil inclination
there is no one who remembers the good inclination.
And the beginning of the stirring
these are those who rule over their inclination;
come, let us calculate the reckoning of the world";
לְהַרְגִּיז הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
of stirring up the good inclination against the evil inclination.
they can break the evil inclination,
as is written in the holy Zohar:
אִתְעַר הַאי כֹּחַ קַדִּישָׁא עִלָּאָה וְכוּלֵּי
"This holy supernal strength is aroused, etc.,
of the Sitra Achra is broken, etc."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א רב, א)
And as is written in the holy Zohar (I 202a):
which is the joining of Chochmah and Binah
which is the inner aspect from Kesser Elyon;
and it is that it should enter the depths of the heart,
so that it remain so forever.
And as is written in the holy Zohar
(פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רמ, א)
זִבְחֵי אֱלֹהִים רוּחַ נִשְׁבָּרָה (תְּהִלִּים נא, יט)
"'The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit' (Tehillim 51:19)
that this impure spirit be broken
one who breaks it as is fitting,
'a spirit that goes and does not return'
that it will never return to him;
this is what is written: 'and does not return.'"
וְזֶהוּ רַק עַל יְדֵי עֵזֶר ה׳
And this is only through the help of Hashem,
וְאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזֵר לוֹ
and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him,
he could not overcome it, etc."
This is from the attribute of Atika,
so that it be "a spirit that goes and does not return";
that is, that it enter the depths of the heart
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרַשִׁ״י (פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא, שְׁמוֹת לא, ג)
And as is written in Rashi (Parshas Ki Sisa, Shemos 31:3):
which shines into him from Kesser Elyon.
And here the verse gives the order
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַדַּעַת הוּא גַּם כֵּן בַּלֵּב
because Daas too is in the heart,
entering the depths of the heart
through the help of the Holy One, blessed be He,
which is "the daughter, from the side of the three levels,"
whoever keeps Shabbos according to its law
as is written in the Gemara (Shabbos 118b)
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (בְּשַׁלַּח, מַסֶּכְתָּא דְּוַיַּסַּע ו)
And as is written in the Mechilta (Beshalach, Vayassa 6):
every "one who keeps Shabbos from profaning it
וְשׁוֹמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ נו, ב)
and keeps his hand from doing any evil" (Yeshayahu 56:2)
is assured and guarded from sin;
and in Pri Etz Chaim the wording is
from the accusation of the evil inclination;
וְאָז הוּא רוּחַ הוֹלֵךְ וְלֹא יָשׁוּב
and then it is "a spirit that goes and does not return."

p: Now, the expression "the strength of Hashem,"
indicate something achieved through fear of Heaven,
as we said in explaining the pasuk
גִּבּוֹר לֹא יִנָּצֵל בְּרָב כֹּחַ (תְּהִלִּים לג, טז)
"A mighty man is not saved by great strength" (Tehillim 33:16):
that this means fear of Heaven.
Seemingly, then, this should have been said
at the meal of Shabbos night,
נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponding to the holiness of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
and not at the second meal,
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
רַק תְּחִלַּת הִתְגַּבְּרוּת עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
But the beginning of overcoming the evil inclination
that it "rise up to the head,"
וּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ בָּא בַּיָּמִים (בְּרֵאשִׁית כד, א)
and of whom it is written "come into days" (Bereishis 24:1)
Although all the Avos presumably merited
to be refined in all the attributes
yet Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
was the first to merit this,
and of him the pasuk states explicitly
may His great Name be blessed'
his decree is torn up for him,
when the people offer themselves willingly, bless Hashem.'
Whoever answers 'Amen' with all his strength,
the gates of Gan Eden are opened for him,
And Rashi explained "with all his strength"
Now this needs to be understood:
the expression "all his strength" for concentration,
גַּם מַה זֶּה לְשׁוֹן כָּל כּוֹחוֹ
and also what is meant by "all" his strength;
רַק אִם כִּוֵּון לִבּוֹ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כט, א)
only "if he directed his heart" (Rosh Hashanah 29a),
כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּכַוְּונוּ לִבָּם לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם (בְּרָכוֹת ל, ב)
"so that they direct their hearts to their Father in Heaven" (Berachos 30b).
(פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רכ, א, הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל)
may His great Name be blessed'
he must arouse all his limbs
And since it says "all his limbs,"
it appears that it explains "all his strength"
עֲרוּכָה בַכֹּל וּשְׁמוּרָה (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כג, ה)
"ordered in all things and secured" (Shmuel II 23:5)
if it is ordered in your two hundred and forty-eight limbs, etc.'"
For if it is in a loud voice,
then it is "ordered" in the two hundred and forty-eight limbs;
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים לה, י)
and this is along the lines of what is said (Tehillim 35:10):
And from the fact that the holy Zohar brings this
on the matter of "to do with your strength"
that rests upon the head of the tzaddikim,
it appears that it explains "with all his strength"
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעַל יְדֵי שֶׁעוֹנֶה בְּקוֹל רָם
That is: by answering in a loud voice,
he is also with all his concentration.
And this is because "all" indicates three
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב הַתּוֹסְפוֹת יוֹם טוֹב סוֹף פָּרָה וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִים)
(as the Tosafos Yom Tov writes at the end of Parah, and the Acharonim);
and this is the meaning of "with all his strength":
with all the first three Sefiros,
that he be refined in these three attributes,
which are reckoning, wisdom and knowledge,
And it says that even with a single word
his decree is likewise torn up
and the gates of Gan Eden are opened for him.
And this is what the holy Zohar says,
אִתְעַר הַאי כֹּחַ קַדִּישָׁא עִלָּאָה כוּ׳
"this holy supernal strength is aroused, etc.,
and the strength and might of the Sitra Achra is broken";
that it will never return to him
"a spirit that goes and does not return,"
as we cited from the holy Zohar
from where they learned in the Gemara,
עַל הָעוֹנֶה אָמֵן יְהֵא שְׁמֵיהּ רַבָּא
about one who answers "Amen, may His great Name be blessed"
for from there one learns only,
that one answers "Amen, may His great Name be blessed,"
but from where "with all his strength"?
Rather, they learned it from what is written "when the people offer themselves willingly";
הוּא עַל מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
refers to the attribute of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who was the first of the converts."
For all the Avos are called generous,
in that they kept the Torah
is in Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who kept it out of the generosity of his heart,
and he had no teacher, etc.";
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is not so of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
שֶׁכְּבָר נוֹלַד מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
who was already born to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who circumcised him at eight days
מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
the attribute of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
"and may it rise up to the head,"
as with Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who merited the attribute of "old, come into days."
And this is what they expounded
from what is written "when the people offer themselves willingly, bless Hashem,"
that it refers to one who answers
אָמֵן יְהֵא שְׁמֵיהּ רַבָּא בְּכָל כּוֹחוֹ
"Amen, may His great Name be blessed" with all his strength;
meaning, with all the first three Sefiros,
the attribute of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
and through this one can merit
that "the holy supernal strength be aroused
and the strength and might of the Sitra Achra be broken."
And so too they expounded from what is written
that it refers to the gates of Gan Eden,
"Open for me the gates of righteousness, etc.;
this is the gate of Hashem,
וְזֶה נֶאֱמַר עַל שַׁעֲרֵי גַּן עֵדֶן
and this was said about the gates of Gan Eden,
וּמִדִּכְתִיב וְיָבֹא גוֹי צַדִּיק (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ כו, ב)
And from what is written "that a righteous nation may enter" (Yeshayahu 26:2)
one who still has a struggle,
who must be a mighty one
(end of the first chapter of Taanis, Taanis 15a):
that is, Hashem Yisbarach sows into the tzaddik
for he still needs the light
in order to overcome his inclination.
And afterward, once he is already called a tzaddik,
that is, he merits uprightness of heart;
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וּלְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא)
as it says: 'and joy for the upright of heart'" (Tehillim 97:11),
as is written (in the Gemara there, Taanis 15a).
And from what is written "a righteous nation"
that is, that he has already merited the first light,
And this is "with all his strength":
with all the first three Sefiros.
And it says that even with a single word
that the gates of Gan Eden be opened for him,
if only it be as it should be,
with all his strength, with all his concentration;
which is with all his limbs.

p: וְהוּזְכְּרוּ אֵלּוּ הַב׳ מַאֲמָרִים הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
These two sayings mentioned above appear
the sayings are on matters of Shabbos;
the connection of these two sayings to this place.
מֵרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and Reish Lakish,
such that these sayings would be mentioned incidentally;
and especially with Amoraim such as these,
who are mentioned many times in Shas,
it is not plausible that the sayings would be mentioned incidentally.
to be with all his strength and with all his concentration.
For on a weekday, too, can merit it
יָכוֹל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִזְכּוֹת לָזֶה
every single Jew can merit this,
for Shabbos is a time of teshuvah,
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem,"
"one who confesses and forsakes will be shown mercy,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר (פֶּרֶק יט)
as is written in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer (chapter 19).
וְשַׁבָּת בַּת מִסִּטְרָא דִּתְלַת דַּרְגִּין עִלָּאִין
And Shabbos is "the daughter, from the side of the three supernal levels,
to be "a spirit that goes and does not return,"
to break the strength and might of the evil inclination,
"a spirit that goes and does not return";
and especially at the second meal,
that of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
whose attribute was generosity and love,
at which one can merit to reach
"may its strength increase and may it rise up to the head."
